review_text: absolutely brilliant game and a beautiful sendoff to one of my favorite series | some key missteps aside dark souls iii is arguably the pinnacle of the series and builds up on everything from software has learned in the ~ years since dark souls came out ~ if we include demon's souls | in short for those of you unfamiliar with the series dark souls iii is a highly atmospheric action-rpg with a heavy emphasis on weighty melee combat or flashy spells if you go that route | while it's set in a fantasy world the world is decayed and bleak to the point where you wouldn't be mistaken for confusing it for an action-horror title | like the previous games in the series dark souls iii is notorious for being brutal but personally it's not that hard once you come to grips with the mechanics and understand how the game wants you to play | dark souls iii like the previous titles has extremely little exposition and cutscenes are sparse so you need to actively read item descriptions and talk to the few npcs that pop up in your journey as well as fill in the missing pieces to get a more complete story | that being said what lore and dialogue that you find are incredibly intriguing and have led to some really creative fan theories shout-out to rdarksouls as for the major differences in dark souls iii compared to the previous games while there are many tweaks to the core gameplay it feels right at home focusing more on refining the formula rather than overhauling it like in dark souls ii | combat in pve is arguably the best in the series | each melee weapon now has more depth since you can now charge heavy melee attacks and perform various weapon arts and the enemy design in this game is really impressive while you have your typical 'doods in armor' you also have some really creepy and disgusting looking enemies very similar in a sense to the monsters in bloodborne | the game's also a lot faster paced since the player's roll got significantly sped up in this game and has a lot of invulnerability frames letting you be really aggressive | on the flip side of the coin enemies are also really aggressive as well so you can't be reckless | if you like boss fights then dark souls iii delivers in spades | dark souls iii really focuses on having aggressive boss fights usually in the form of duels though there are some extremely large boss fights though these tend to be gimmicky and not all that enjoyable and they're an absolute blast | i'd say that there are few bad boss fights in this game with over half of the bosses in all players | magic miracles and pyromancy have all been massivlely improved with two simple additions | instead of the unwieldy method that was previously used where a spellcaster would need to equip be a step closer the bloodborne style combat but not too many steps away from dark souls | the inclusion of special attacks and a bar which limits magic attacks has helped make play more varied and helps limit what is often considered 'cheesing' your way through the game | the method of storytelling is as always awesomely opaque with hints slipped into the fabric of the world for you to discover | the world itself appears to be a return to what people liked so much about ds whilst appeared to be the primary weakness of the second game independent of the dlc which seemed to be made more congruently | the game i would say is visually stunning in its environments but also in its boss fights par a few bad early ones | with a gtx and a middle of the range processor the game runs reasonably smooth and have only experienced one game crash so far from hours of gameplay and in its early days | though i'm really pleased with the game i am a bit disappointed with a few things | the replayability of the game appears to now be based on unlocking side quests which makes your actions very consequential and likely will have to be planned with the specific purpose of completing these quests which i do find quite annoying as it seems like too much of a push to ng plus though suppose it worked on me having done a fair few playthroughs just for this reason but still i feel a bit cheated | the story is however excellent as always and remains consistent between games | there is a sort of meeting of features of all the different games into this one almost like a love letter to all their previous creations; and appears to be a great send off to the series in this way | unfortunately there is the subtraction of some things which worked excellently in ds: such as dual wielding which seemed to provide more depth to combat; and the fight arena though the latter perhaps done with fair reason so to make the game world feel more congruous and less disjointed which was the fatal flaw of the second game | they also didn't implement differences between new game and subsequent playthroughs in the way of 'red phantoms' and increased numbers of enemies as well as increased enemy strength which was implemented very well again in ds but not as far as i know ds and added variation and difficulty to further playthroughs with increasing challenge | in dark souls unfortunately i am implemented often as a general rule even in games which require considerably less time investment | but to this point having done a couple of runs through the game i couldn't of asked much more from it i usually moan at full price games but it has been very much worth every penny and i am greatly looking forward to its dlc which if anything like previous games will be absolutely amazing | keep it up from software

review_text: ever since playing the first fallout back in ' i've been hooked and played every fo game a number of times since | now i have been known to approach the fo line with rose-colored glasses but i can honestly say that this is the first one that actually makes me feel like i'm fighting the struggle i'd expect to have in a post-nuclear apocalypse wasteland | first the fact that you actually have to collect junk when you're out and about assuming of course you're into the settlement building which we'll get into in a minute is fantastic | i'd expect to have to scavenge for things in the wasteland | in all previous fallout games junk was just a way to line your bank account with sweet sweet caps | now i find myself having to go out to find things i scan scavenge screws crystals and adhesives for | just like i'd expect it to be if i were roaming the wastes every damn roll of duct tape has got to come back with me | secondly and perhaps the best change to make you actually feel the post-nuclear part is that rad damage actually hurts | sure in the past games you could grow additional appendages by getting enough rads and at certain levels you'd get hit with a debuff but in all previous fo's i haven't had to care much at all about rads | not the case | rad-x and radaways are my number one stocked chem aside from stimpacks | i mean the whole world got nuked | shouldn't you have to actually fear the radiation | easily my most favorite part in this game though is the settlement building | there's just something about having to build settlements for settlers some of them with names and stories that really entices me | minecraft never really did it for me; fallout as of yet | so here we go | pros: environmental graphics quality is an aspect of fallout that easily adds to the overall quality of the game | environmental changes: radiation storms that blow in from the west occasional rain storms sun riseset cloudy daysnights and starry nights can add to the aesthetically pleasing scenery of the game or can alter your gameplay difficulty | animalcreature movement scare enemy drugs jet mentats buffout and more | cooking stations provide uses for animalhumanmutant body parts you pick up cook and consume radiation resistace increased health for a as if you are bringing the modern era to an old-west town give orders to your settlers to work on resources or defend the town settlements can be attacked by raiders super mutants and gouls adding review_text: having sunk close to hours at the time of this review and undoubtedly more to come with another expansion on the way i've largely enjoyed my journey in the game can summarize my time with fallout as 'mostly positive' but there definitely are some glaring flaws and issues with the game | pro's: the game world bethesda has yet again created a gorgeous atmospheric game world that is truly the best part of the game | you can set out in any direction and come across beautifully detailed and exciting locationscompounds and other interesting locations | equally filled with action and for those more detail oriented compelling stories of the remnants of pre-war life via various terminals and documentation | the best adventures for me came from experiences not within my quest journal | gameplay didn't run really any melee so i can't really comment on that but the gunplay felt incredibly smooth and enjoyable | with a wide range of customization for gunsarmorpower armor you could really nail down what type of approach you wanted to take and make it work around your playstyle | companions i really loved how they handled companions in this game and imo ended up being the best characters of the game | strong distinct personalities and skillsets that would change and open up to as they became more familiar and trusting of you | companions stopping you during your journey to simply discuss things going on in their life was surprisingly always a treat for me and made them and the world around them feel a little bit more real | add that to the fact nearly all of them also have quests that involve their backgroundhistory that unlock as they grow more fond of you and you can feel yourself grow more close | match that with the fact that majority of them can also open up romantic love interest dynamics and a wide variety of different companions for every play style and you got a really well-done addition | far harbor bethesda has a track record of outstanding near full length games quality dlc and that was the same in this instance | they really knocked it out of the park with beautifully crafted atmospheric 'bar harbor' maine filled to brim with vast locations unique distinct personalitiesfactions and tons of great choices and decisions to make | honestly probably the best rpg decisions in the entirety of the game i experienced there | fantastic job from there there | modding community as with any bethesda game the allowed and focused upon involvement of mods makes this another huge positive | they are vast and extremely devoted and talented | an absolute highlight of any bethesda game and truly benefit the game immensely | seeing as this is a pc review it's definitley worth mentioning and the future is always evolving and promising with mods | i wish more devs would follow suite and do this | neutral: quests i put this here because i'm honestly a bit torn | the 'real' quests that actually were written i felt were actually pretty well done and immersive | choosing between different factions allies and decisions alot of times really had me sitting there game paused going back and forth in my mind weighing what i really wanted to do | factions were really nice in the sense that they avoided the terrible good guybad guy cliche and really made all of them seem more gray and realistic | everybody had their positives and everybody had their own skeletons in the closet that made them seem shadyunappealing | the debates you can find with fans debating who is best for the commonwealth is a testament to that | so why have i put this under neutral if i felt the quality was good | because of the quantity | unfortunately it feels like you run out of the 'real' quests somewhat quickly and find yourself in radiant quest purgatory | now i have no problem with radiant quests they add a little objective and incentive to go out and explore but they should never act as the main substitute of questing and unfortunately it feels like they are way too frequent and common as compared to the non-repeatable quests | buildingconstructionsettlements i put this under neutral for one reason | with my own personal bias i absolutely love this addition to the game | i'm the type of guy who spent countless hours in games like mcsims etc creating and building | i absolutely love this and one of my favorite aspects of fallout was creating my own unique and extremely detailed settlements and communities writing the backstory and history of them | it was incredibly enjoyable from a creativity and immersion standpoint | the system is well done and provides lots of different materials and objects for you to use | this only increases tenfold with the addition of mods who really open up building to a whole new level | again you may be wondering why i put this as neutral | because quite simply it's highly subjective | there is a large crowd who don't want this addition and feels it has no place in this type of game and if you are one of those people you will find this quite unappealing because construction and settlements play and gigantic role in this game | of the dlc focus and are dedicated to this feature and it is a big part of the feel and play of the game | so it's really a matter of whether or not you enjoy this type of gameplay or not | if you do your in for a treat | if not you'll grow to despise it | negative: repetitive nature of end-game: again this kinda harps on the quests topic but i feel like it's worth mentioning again and not in a positive light | the main quest and various 'real' sidequests will provide a good amount of fun exciting content and the landmass dlc's provide even more but when they are all wrapped up and completed you will be at the mercy of the sandbox | which for many is enjoyable given the incredibly detailed and well-done world but will eventually grow tiring | your endgame will consist of maintaining and growing settlements and exploring the various locations of the world solely for the purpose of explorative enjoyement and suppliesmaterialsresources | radiant quests help in this regard but given how early on you encounter them you may find yourself avoiding anything radiant like the plague | dialogue system now i will say i disagree with alot of the comments that you cant be evil because that is definitely untrue | you can be a grade a and downright evil if you want to selling children to slavery keeping cures to yourself and leaving kids to die betrayal robbing murdering lying and all the goodness of being a baddie galore and much more | the only difference you don't get a pop-up that reminds you that you were naughty | however the dialoguevoiced antagonist was an absolute disaster | nothing against the voice actor himselfherself they had lovely voices but it severely limited options and selection dialogue wheel was very limiting and quite frankly a failed effort | bethesda has even acknowledged they know they made a mistake and it went poorly and good on them for it | so hopefully it will be a case of 'tried it and learned our lesson' and won't see it in the future however in the case of this game it is definitley worth mentioning | especially when you consider the quality of dialogue found in games such as witcher | in summary i had an absolute blast with the game and it has kept me invigorated and playing for a long time and the future still looks bright with one more major dlc on the way and the modding community | there are a few glaring issues and omissions from the game and quite frankly your enjoyement could very well come down to your subjective preferences and likings when it comes to structured railsopen gameplay | it's story shines at points but it's certainly not witcher levels of a great main questline | to any who enjoy a beautifully crafted invigorating and incredibly detailed open world with creative outlets you will like | final rating:

liked the branching story paths unpredictability and the ability to solve problems without violence that the previous games had | none of which are found in this one | while the new weapon mods system is great as is the new power armor system everything else falls short | and a lot of things made no sense | after a battle fought in power armor parts had to be fixed since a grenade fell nearby | understandable but if you fight the same battle in raider armor made from junk you never need to fix it | weapons also never break weaken or jam even those made from plumbing supplies and driftwood | which oddly enough describes half the guns in this game | the build system lacks physics making it possible to build bases that hover in the air | and they have a crippling parts count limit that seems pretty arbitrary | the game is small both in size and density | there are towns with voiced characters | everywhere else is populated by raiders | skyrim had believably large cities and several more towns | all with voiced characters and many side quests new vegas had at least | even fallout had such locations | most fallout side quests use repetitive dialogue especially the minutemen ones | and nearly all consist of nothing more than going somewhere and killing or fetching something | gone too is the humor these quests brought in previous titles | the story relies on a series of twilight zone style twists | which of course are no fun the next time | dialogue options are limited and you don't actually know what your own character is going to say | perks have no effect on dialogue at all and neither does the special | the background given to your character if they are male is that there a war veteran while if your female you're a lawyer and yet the story progresses exactly the same | despite most of it involving killing people | come on since she is voiced and a lawyer; i expected her to be a little upset after killing somebody the first time but | nope | she didn't even react to facing a deathclaw which also happens in the first min | why they didn't just have whoever you choose be the ex soldier i don't know it would have made more sense | especially since you get your first power armor within the first minutes and know how to work it something a lawyer turned housewife should not know how to do | the largest gripe of all i had is in nearly every quest nothing you do matters | you can talk somebody out of killing a person only to have their partner do it anyway with the dialogue after being identical | no choice you make in a quest has any repercussions later | in fact there is no karma system or even a bounty system like skyrim | you can walk into town kill guards come back a few days later and they're back to cracking jokes about your armor | in general the game doesn't really let you be evil no mater how many people you kill or what quest options you choose folks will treat you as their savior | no hidden faction or missions are revealed for your misdeeds unlike the previous fallout's or skyrim | unlike new vegas you can't broker alliances between factions | worst of all no matter who you side with you get the same end missions | many of which share animations scenes and objectives | followed by the same monologue and montage after | despite having radically different agendas all factions resort to the same exact methods | making every choice you thought you made meaningless | which is why i agree with many others in saying that this is an fps game | not even a particularly good one |

review_text: just a quick note: i own none of the dlc this game was in development for so long and somehow it still feels incomplete | oh sure you can build up your settlements have crops and defense and structures but most of the time it's just downright frustrating to do any of that | there's no grid to snap walls floors or anything to | the only time they snap is to another wall or floor and why is it that cables have this predetermined curve to them causing them to sometimes be unplaceable because the curve passes through the ground or something when in reality that's not at all what would happen | and why when i'm building can't i float around like i've turned off collision so i don't have to build a set of stairs just to be able to put something up on a roof | the variety of enemies from previous titles is gone | new vegas gave the player a vast and easily encountered number of different factions | in fallout the majority of enemy factions basically comes down to ghouls which the game even sometimes reminds the player during a random loading screen are not zombies super mutants and raiders | occasionally the player will have to deal with gunners and during the more story-driven quests synths but that's about it | those are the most common enemies in the game and they're the most common by quite a lot | of course it's possible this wouldn't be so bothersome if it weren't for the fact that by its own design the game forces these enemy factions to be encountered extremely often | there is an abysmal amount of side quests in this game as it seems instead focus has been placed on giving the player repeatable quests to either defend a settlement by building up its defenses help a settlement get one of its members back after they were kidnapped usually by a settlement of raiders somewhere clear out a location filled with ghouls or stop super mutants from raiding a settlement again by clearing them out of a location too | wash rinse repeat indefinitely | when i walked onto a pier and randomly discovered the 'here there be monsters' quest i nearly cried at the thought of being able to do something other than clear out a dungeon | the skill system has been absolutely decimated | there are no more skills | now there are only perks | one weakness i've found of the fallout games has always been that they never really hammer home any sense of really building your character into one specific thing | you have the ability to put points into whatever skills you want resulting in just making your character generally better at everything | some people really like this and i can understand that completely but never was the problem with this system so glaring until now | skills have turned into perks and also perks are still perks | the guns skill has now been broken up and scattered all over the tree into several different perks whereas before there were not only perks relating to guns but a skill designated for them too | some of these new perks however are just completely pointless | lockpicking for example progresses exactly as it used to except now because everything is locked to a certain level it's impossible to be able to open master locks until a certain level is achieved which makes no sense and makes the whole system feel incredibly watered down | in previous games you could just max out any skill as quickly as you desired | it makes leveling feel unrewarding as your choices in what you can do have become way more limited | one positive thing i'd like to mention is the very creative way that junk works | you can now pick up pretty much any item you find and sell it or store it at a workbench and use its base materials to help you build things around your settlements | it's a very nice way to give a bit more interactivity to the world the player is in as it allows you to do more with those objects than just pick them up and toss them around | overall despite everything i've said this is still a fun game though i can't really play it for many hours at a time due to the never-ending bombardment of settlement quests | the weapon and armor customization is really good though it is annoying being forced to wait until a certain level so the next rank of the armorer or science perk can be met in order to do more things with the customizing | the story isn't half bad even if it is a bit short and the outside environments are fantastic as long as you don't look to closely at them | however i still can't recommend this game for the detailed reasons above as well as some other minor things unfinished roofs building textures warping into each other the super mutants voices have somehow gotten even more irritating etc | hopefully the next fallout will be able to fix at least some of these problems |

review_text: there is a lot i want to say about this game and the series | the first game i played in this series was fallout and i enjoyed it | i enjoyed it for what it was it wasn't great but i had fun | i didn't play new vegas for a long time after it came out because i had heard that it was just like fo and while i enjoyed it was nothing special | when i finally got around to playing nv and realized how masterfully it was crafted i couldn't help but think to myself 'this is what an rpg should be like | ' i found myself immersed in the world in such a natural way | so many distinctive characters that i can still remember with stories that pulled my heart strings | both the stories of the individuals and the different factions and tribes were not only extremely well threshed out but interwoven to form a cohesive whole | the stories of the dlc even were masterfully woven in there were hints and stories of big mt the sierra madre hotel the burning man and the other courier put into the main game so when you got to them it just felt natural | i won't go into detail because this isn't a new vegas review but the story was amazing the faction system the completely intuitive crafting system and an extremely well made perk system that encouraged you to specialize and thus role-play | everything worked together to suck you into the game | so i thought 'bethesda will definitely see how much their fans like this and keep to this formula right | i mean surely they can play it themselves and see how much it surpasses fo as a game and as a story i mean obsidian games knocked it out of the park | ' sadly though i was disappointed | a leveling system that stripped away almost all role-playing elements | a terrible conversation system that still brought back the stupid percentile chance persuasion check system that almost everybody hated the mod that fixed it was one of the top on the nexus | bethesda did not learn from nv they seem to have lost sight of what it means make an rpg and that makes me sad because i have been a fan of theirs for a long time | i really do like parts of the game | deacon and nick valentine are incredible characters with a lot of depth | piper while interesting fell kinda flat | i really liked finding locations like the u | s | s constitution | captain ironsides and his conflict with the scavengers was an incredibly fun and funny part of the game | if only more locations felt like that instead of procedurally generated dungeons with the same generic baddies re-hashed over and over again | muties ghouls or raiders | the baddies in nv were not only more diverse but they all had a back story | the four different raider factions all had a story and by playing certain quests you learn about and interact with them in ways other than shooting them in the head | another thing many of the conflicts in the game had a non-violent solution | it was completely possible to beat the game with zero kills and as you got to know some of the factions that were considered 'bad' like the great khans you might not wish to kill them anymore | none of the raiders that i have come across in my time playing fallout have felt real like that | they're just cardboard cutouts for me to shoot with bullets and laser beams | why are there no options for me to use the special stats in conversation | i chose to have high intelligence because i like the choices it gave me in nv and the only thing it gave me was earlier access to some perks and in the one quest with the u | s | s constitution i mentioned i got to keep some cables and repair some stuff easier | wow | of course there are no skills anymore so no need to even mention using them | i don't hate this game i have enjoyed playing it and will most likely still enjoy playing it but this was the only way i could make my dissatisfaction known | i wish steam had a neutral review so i could do that instead | if i had played this without playing new vegas i probably would have enjoyed it more but as it stands i was expecting bethesda to use new vegas as an example and build on the work of obsidian games to make a bigger and better fallout | new vegas wasn't perfect there was certainly room for improvement | instead bethesda made this and i can't help but feel disappointed | bethesda if any of you are reading this however unlikely that might be please note that i don't think you should quit making fallout games | rather listen to the outcry in the community that follows it | we would rather have a game in a smaller world that it fully threshed out than a big one that feels so empty |

review_text: edit: at hours so far i think i can review the game in its entirety | this will be a long review since i'll be comparing fallout to the two previous bethesda installments | a tl;dr can be found near the bottom | i loved fallout | it explored a world last left alone by interplay a good number of years ago | it came back around via bethesda's production and imagination bringing you an unpretty post-apocalyptic experience | it let players explore the game in their own right making moral questions along their experience | fallout: new vegas took from the atmosphere of fo and expanded upon that | i grew to love nv even more than fo | not only did it capture the fallout universe even more but the gameplay mechanics were far more intuitive and expansive | with that being said i strongly like fallout but quite can't love it in its current state | as a fallout game it's not as good as the previous two games released by bethesda | i like to think of it in the same vein as dark souls versus dark souls : the second game was great in its own right but the overall experience was largely forgettable compared to the first one | ----------- for the cons: fallout feels very watered down and shallow compared to the previous games | they discarded the karma system and skill levels | everything having to do with improving your character's abilities is done solely by perks | while the other games' perks felt exactly like the definition of the word a system complementing one's play-style now it's a forced simplified leveling system | the skill levels of past games influenced passive traits and skill checks helping a player notice their character change and grow in subtle ways within the overall world | i was hoping the leveling system was a bit similar to skyrim: while it wasn't perfect your skills increased based on actions made in real-time and you could only choose certain perks after reaching certain skill levels | carrying the simplified theme there are only main factions in this new installment with several other minor factions that largely don't interact with you other than simply having to kill them | previous installments didn't necessarily have more per se but you could choose how you could interact with them | in fallout you could either side or go against certain factions and actually interact with them | in fallout: nv you could be more diplomatic and choose whether certain minor factions ally or become enemies with certain major factions | in fallout it's simply kill-on-sight save for a couple minor factions which don't add to the bigger picture | as a consequence the world feels ironically less alive | while fallout is larger than the other games' maps the lack of independent settlements doesn't make it feel like you're stepping into a different world | i suppose that was bethesda's way of showing that it's still a post-apocalyptic setting but the other games' populations made you feel like they were struggling to survive | this game simply feels empty | the quests in this game aside from the main quests suffer from the redundant quests commonly found in mmorpgs go kill this enemy or retrieve this item return receive xp and repeat said formula | no depth no interesting side story just errands | the lack of a karma system means you can't feel your character make decisions contributing to their overall moral standpoint | other reviewers touched on the fact you can only choose four options within context-sensitive dialogue | in my opinion it isn't that the four options aren't inherently bad in their own right but that the four options don't really contribute to any long-lasting consequences or effects | aside from ultimately deciding which of the four major factions you side with you eventually have to agree with most characters whether you want to or not | ------- now for some good points which are still somewhat partial: the crafting system is interesting | you can mod weapons armor and clothing which takes some influence from skyrim | depending on your play-style you can customize your character to be more stealth-based full-melee a heavy gunner or a hybrid | it gives you many different ways to play that aren't as initially apparent | the settlement-building system is one point i liked | it's a bit janky initially as certain pieces don't lock into certain places | however it can be mostly optional if you choose to play that way | it feels like you're actually rebuilding the commonwealth | it wasn't fully hashed out in my opinion because settler management can get annoying | the only way to tell who is assigned to what is by seeing it in first-person via line-of-sight as opposed to a menu showing the breakdown of the system in play | however i can appreciate bethesda's ambitions on settlement-building so it's not quite a con to me | with certain perks you can link your settlements together and see your control grow over the commonwealth | what fallout lacks in expansiveness among multiple factions and faction interaction it excels in your ultimate choice on which major faction to side with | there are no inherently good or bad factions your decisions depending on the type of person you are will take some time and consideration | the leveling system goes on indefinitely too | while i hate the redesigned perkleveling system it seems to have been put in place with the thought in mind that one could play indefinitely and continuously improve your character | i like that it's so gradual that you never feel like you're done with your character | a weird consequence in my own experience is that the beginning of the game feels harder than other games then you reach a particular plateau where you end up steamrolling over everything then it becomes hard again when your weapons no longer do as much damage to higher-leveled enemies forcing one to have to adapt their play-style accordingly | i personally like leveling in that aspect | combat in this game is a clear winner over previous games | vats moves slowly as opposing to pausing causing you to make quick decisions on where you hit your targets | weapons feel like actual weapons versus being just weapon models | revamping power armor was a very nice touch | they feel heavy powerful and you can customize them to nearly any play-style as well | the graphics are quite pretty | from my standpoint i think it'll depend on how you feel about it within the context of the game | fallout and new vegas now looks slightly dated compared to fallout but in my opinion they captured the roughness of a post-apocalyptic environment | this game while very pretty doesn't look like the aftermath of a nuclear attack | ----- overalltl;dr: fallout is a good game in its own right if you're new coming into the fallout universe | very accessible to the new player without getting too complex | if you played fallout and new vegas this new game isn't necessarily bad it's still a fun game but the features that became staples in the previous installments were either simplified or left behind | i still recommend this game because ultimately it's a fun game | i loved fallout and new vegas; i review_text: something about the beth-rpg is so pure innocent and addictingly fun they're impossible to put down impossible to not appreciate | the problem is fallout is deeply flawed regardless of my boundless love and addiction for it | as a rabid fan of obsidian's superb new vegas i've realised the 'formula' for the beth-rpg is bulletproof | what cannot be replicated is the nuance of the true avatars and world of an rpg | fallout unfortunately lacks many of the rpg mechanics of it's predecessors and is far more in line with a borderlands title | it's a 'looter-shooter' where you upgrade customize your guns find new ones and explore a gorgeous world | all negativity aside | it's a fun addicting fps with an expansive open world | aesthetic she ain't a looker as far as texture resolution and overall graphical power goes | blurry close-up textures aside the overall presentation is actually fantastic | the world is colorful and intricately designed from curving futuristic skyscrapers to decrepit wooden shacks with streams of fabric tied around the beams to verdant trash laden radioactive plains and clawing nuclear winter trees | character models are actually capable of expressing emotion | lighting is superb with glorious sunsets casting god rays through trees or the glaring illumination and stark shadows of fenways spotlights | there is also an impressive shamble and clutter to crumbling city streets or shot laden bars | gun models are satisfactory with appropriately complex laser weaponry gleaming blades gunpower stained firearms and plenty of random knobs and buckles alongside glowing sights | youll see tons of 'holy-' vistas and even some crowded bullet riddled rooms you can slowly pan around as a candle burns in the corner and desk fans shadow whirls on a nuka cola poster studded wall | sound guns sound fine | nice crack crisp explosion blunt strike perfectly satisfactory | the wasteland eerily quiet with bursts of distant gunfire and screams of terrifying wildlife haunting the silence | stalking through buildings is accompanied by crackling fires and hummin electricity urban areas have appropriate bustle | a huge letdown however is the radio | little new songs were added | i actually turned the radio off and am so glad i did because the ambient score is criminally underappreciated | the soft piano of wasteland travel is both unsettling and hopeful while combat is heavily drummed and quickens the pulse immediately | faction themes are especially notable from the heroic horn of the brotherhood to furtive and optimistic electronica of the railroad | im listening to it as i write in fact | combat fps gameplay is revamped and drastically improved from previous games | aside from more nimble aiming and hady kickback from big guns general motion is far smoother and more human than nv and | peaking from cover to empty a rifle mag from the hip at an enemy has never felt better more so when you sprint forward to smack him across the head with the stock and once more onto his kneeling back | the ai of npcs has improved with enemies and companions scrounging for more effective weapons utilizing turrets and grenades flanking sticking to cover suppressing and creating actual search patterns with chilling dialogue too | as a rule of thumb enemies with visible armour pieces bosses and legendaries who drop cool status effect off and still clawing their way across the ground stumps bleedingsparking gave me a sadistic pleasure | guns are diverse with a variety of models and different handling characteristics | roaring shotguns cracking accurate rifles the maelstrom of lead spewing minigun fiery beam lasers blunt and brutal sledgehammers and the horse-kick and flinging impact of a heavy assault rifle | you can also equip your avatar with a variety of creative clothing and armour both for aesthetic and damage protection | power-armour also know functions as a mech with satisfyingly heavy steps hulking mass and resistance to bullets | crafting is also expansive with firearms and armour hosting a score of attachments from extended mags and holo sights to bayonets extra pockets or electric charge | unfortunately thats it | combat consists of armouring up shooting your way through a swarm of enemies trading hp hits with the inevitable boss then bringing home your loot to customize your guns | there are few detective missions diplomatic meetings or hostage rescues quests simply lack the variety and options of approach of prior games | there is no option to sneak through and pickpocket the card key hot wire the vents to close or even convince the enemy to give up | shoot loot and upgrade | setting as usual bethesda knocked it out of the park | specifically fenway park converted into the crowded and ramshackle diamond city populated by catchers mask and pad wearing guards and a center square surrounded by shops with names like home plate | the commonwealth is a terrifically realised world brimming with creative passion from the fleshed-out characters within to the intricately crafted locales | companions are especially impressive and return to the new vegas character progression of old | inquisitive and feisty reporters wise cracking cyborg-detectives or naive killer-robot french | medics | the map is massive and varied from the quaint woods and towns of northern concord down to the commercial high rise-sprawl of downtown boston heading either too the crowded suburbs and docks near the south end or swampy horror of witch trial salem | those of the more adventurous sort can hazmat suit up and head to the glowing sea a radioactive-electric stormed-smoldering-deathclaw ridden hell | scrounge for parts to build up your own settlement with a simply and somewhat intuitive settlement building system | choose from pre-built houses assemble your own from walls and roofs fill it with comfy chairs spotlights machinegun turrets guard towers and walls | build a recruiting beacon and watch as potential merchants farmers and security drift in | you can build some surprisingly comfortable and sprawling outposts with the tools provided | but ultimately my experience in fallout was flawed | in pursuit of an amazing open world and tuned combat the gave up the rpg mechanics which had initially made me love the series | gone are numerous dialogue options replaced by an overly-simplified but voice-acted and well mere options | yes no more info and sarcastic | no longer can my character be charming cunning evil devious hopeful authoritative charismatic romantic ect | this is further worsened by the new skill system | instead of assigning points to categories which unlocked new dialogue or abilities through mastery you are limited to a perk chart | assign points to sets of perks which are arbitrarily assigned to primary attributes you must master to unlock said perks | want to be a stealthy sniper | good luck | your rifle accuracy is determined through a perception perk your headshot chance through a luck perk your damage and stealthiness through some agility perks and your ability to craft a weapon through intelligence perks | honestly i loved my time with this game | i ache for the return of fully realised rpg systems and the death of the dialogue tree | but more so i appreciate the graphical overhaul incredible world and fine-tuned combat | review_text: overall i'd say this is a game worth getting | it may not be worth $ but it's still strong and i don't feel bad that i spent money on it | pros: the story: this game has one of the best stories an action game has had in recent memory | it's nice to play as a black war veteran anti-hero it's a direction that hasn't been taken in many games in the past | it also features a cast of interesting characters at least the ones of any significance to the story | without spoiling too much the high point of the story is definitely the confrontation at the end between clay and the villain; it is realistically one of my favorite moments in any video game | the story isn't perfect it isn't as good as mafia ii's story and is sadly spread too far and few between by an abundance of repetitive and unskippable story missions that don't actually progress the plot | overall though the story and characters are so well written that it has to be a plus | combat: combat is definitely improved in this game over its predecessors | the inclusion of the stealth and brutal execution mechanics are key points which make this a fun game to play | nothing is more satisfying than brutally stabbing a mafiosa repeatedly in the face and then taking out his startled friend with a close range shotgun to the gut that sends him ragdolling back through the air | there is also a great amount of flexibility in the combat tactics you can use in the game | stealth going in guns-a-blazing and any mixture of the two are all valid and useable combat tactics in mafia iii | it also is really rewarding to stealth through one of the racket missions just to sneak up on the man in charge and grab him before he knows what's going on | i do need to make note that the ai is pretty stupid especialy when it comes to the stealth; they will often times look right past you and you can make them throw caution to the wind with a simple whistle to draw them to an area where you can stealth kill them with a simple press of the 'q' key | the flexibility doesn't just come in tactics either | there are a wide range of weapons and explosives to choose from | although it is kind of lame that you have very limited ammo supplies even with the upgrades and additionally can only carry two weapons one small arms and one large arms weapon | i found myself often times dropping the extremely overpriced weapons i had bought purely out of the lack of ammo supply | regardless of these small issues the combat definitely felt improved over mafia ii | exploration: exploring new bordeaux in mafia iii is a lot of fun | each area feels pretty different from any of the others which is crazy considering there are different areas in the city | while exploration isn't very fruitful aside from gathering collectibles see cons it is still enjoyable for explorations sake | if you want to be rewarded tangibly for exploring you may not enjoy the exploration but if you just enjoy virtual site seeing you'll have a good time | soundtrack: the soundtrack is great | while i prefered mafia ii's soundtrack jazz is my jam the use of classic rock songs at specific points of the game was great | health and armor worked were also pretty unbalanced and annoying | fully upgraded you have four health bars but getting shot with a shotgun puts you down to about half of a bar and then only that bar will refill unless you use medicine which is extra annoying because the game insists on making medicine hard to come by when you need it and expensive to buy for how often you need to use it for it to be effective | similarly the armor that you spent $ on would disappear after a shotgun shot and pistol shot combined | while it may be helpful in a few situations on the whole it doesn't really do too review_text: i try to be an optimist in my life as much as possible | i dont find it enjoyable to be a pessimist and be cynical about everything | thats why im going to try and look at mafia iii as a glass-half-full kind of game | the good parts of mafia are really tremendous but the bad parts are equally as frustrating | mafia iii follows the dare i say it underrated mafia ii released in | mafia ii followed the story of vito scaletta as he rose through the ranks of the mob and told a really compelling and gripping story | the narrative was tight with great characters but had one nearly universal criticism; the gameplay | mafia ii was an open world game that didnt need to be open world | there were prolonged amounts of having to drive from point a to b with no real reason to do so | you couldnt interact with the rest of the world and there was nothing else to see so it was literally just a waste of time | unfortunately mafia iii follows this same path | mafia iii takes place in fictional louisiana in with the biracial vietnam vet lincoln clay in the lead role | thats a lot to digest right there; late s racism the vietnam war | mafia iii puts a whole heck of a lot on its plate and attempts to finish it all | i would say that the devs at hangar do quite a deft job of navigating the themes and issues of the time while taking them head on without beating you over the head with it or coming off as offensive | their depiction of racism during this time is done in a believable way | yes there is a gratuitous amount of racial slurs thrown around but as the disclaimer at the beginning of the game says its done to be accurate to the times and not to diminish or shy away from what people went through | the characterization in mafia iii is really great giving you characters you can empathize with as well as ones that you loathe | they give lincoln clay an interesting backstory and mostly make great use of it in a revenge story that doesnt feel clich | mafia iiis story provides a great foundation yet its the games design that really shows its cracks | now i know that game design is a tough job and i dont want to come across like an armchair quarterback but the mission designer really dropped the ball here | with the exception of a handful the majority of the mission structures in mafia are exactly the same | you need to weaken a racket so you go to [insert building here] and either kill or interrogate the boss at that site as well as destroy any contraband and take any money thats there | while there are permutations and different settings thats effectively what the game is | i think it goes without saying that it can get a tad bit monotonous | thankfully the gunplay and the stealth are good enough that you can mix up and vary your play style to keep things from getting stale | i was specifically impressed by how viable of an option the stealth was which is almost unheard of in a gta-style open world game | there were numerous missions where i ghosted the whole place and didnt fire a single shot | the other design choice that left me scratching my head was no fast travel | its what the hell | now im not necessarily for games being easier i know some people appreciate hard games but what i have little to no tolerance for is a game that wastes my time | the developers here seemingly left out fast travel for no other reason than to pad the games length | much like mafia ii theres no reason for me to stop anywhere while im driving to a destination | my eyes nearly got stuck the amount of times i rolled them back as the game wanted me to go from one side of the map to the other | thats simply insulting to me as a consumer | i will say though that the driving is damn fun | perhaps the best open world driving ive experienced | so while i may have complaints with the lack of fast travel having to drive everywhere didnt really wear on me until the very end because the car handling was so sublime | mafia iii was a game that i was hoping would be in my goty discussion | sadly its not there and its not even particularly close | but that does not mean that its a bad game | the narrative and the characters that are presented are top notch and are what kept me coming back and driving literally through the so-so gameplay to reach its finale | i recommend people play mafia iii because without sounding trite its a bold and brave move for a aaa game to have a black protagonist and deal with the themes and issues that it does | but with that recommendation comes a caveat; know what youre getting into | if you think that the nature of the mission structure will not bother you then there is a ton of fun to be had here | is it worth $ | absolutely not but if you can get it around $ then i think theres enough there to satisfy | i wouldnt have played it for hours had i not enjoyed it |

review_text: mafia iii is an exercise in tedium | the first couple of hours are decent then the story grinds to a halt as the player is tasked with taking over different rackets and districts of the city | this makes up the large majority of the game and involves you driving between repetitive filler-tier activities that take less time to complete than it does to drive over to them | it's a shame because the handful of properly-designed missions that are in the game are fairly decent | the combat is pretty slick the enemies have good hit reactions to gunfire and the gunfights can be quite fast-paced with the mouse and keyboard controls | most of the gunfights in the game will last about thirty seconds to a minute though considering the repetitive racket-takeover missions make up most of the time | the game has a fair number of bugs too | a few times i'd have to restart missions from a checkpoint because it bugged out and i couldn't progress | if you shoot and kill an enemy near a railing they'll play an animation where they fall over the railing but they'd often freeze at the point where the canned animation was supposed to transition to ragdoll physics so they'd end up suspended in mid-air | if you have police chasing you and you call in the favour to get rid of the cops they'll literally disappear right in front of you | the optimisation is an issue also | in my experience they actually fixed the game up and had it running quite well through post-launch patches but with the latest update the one that introduces racing and car customisation they seem to have reverted all of these optimisations and the game runs like crap again | you can't roll-back to previous builds through steam either so the only way to play the game with good performance now is to download a cracked version of the last build which is absolutely ridiculous | overall on the plus side the game has a nice soundtrack and world; decent characters and acting; and good combat | on the other hand there are only a few good missions hidden amongst hours of absolute tedium; there are bugs; and the latest build screwed up the performance | would only recommend this if you can get it super cheap and you're willing to accept the risk of possibly slipping in to a coma from mind-numbingly boring missions |

play at some point in most of the levels | additionally the game forces even more death-match style of kamakaze engagement by sometimes having a timed element | for example at one point you are trapped in a fairly small area with limited cover and have to protect a wheeled-drone type of tank from rpgs while being shot at by the entire korean army | unless you kill enough of the rpg-shooters the tank is destroyed forcing a restart of the level | there is no option but to run-and-gun suffering a lot of damage from the korean army while trying to get enough of the rpgs to pass the level | if you like the deathmatch style of playing against tons of bots then you may like homefront | for me frequently being forced into this style of play is one of the elements that end up being frustrating rather than fun | to make it worse during these frantic engagements one of your team-mates continues to repeat some instruction maybe as a 'hint' | for example in the rpg scenario he will repeat over and over 'get the rpg in the third floor window' or ' | on the rooftop' | this extremely loud repetition becomes so irritating that i played the last couple of tries with the sound muted | following are some other game-play related issues: the character control seems very sluggish compared to other shooters- almost like playing in slightly slow motion while the rest of the game is normal speed | jumping up from a crouch is about half the speed of the enemies who jump from behind cover to shoot | this is especially frustrating as there is no leaning implemented in the game | so you have to jump up from behind cover in slow motion getting shot a couple of times before you are even up | you can only jump the equivalent of about a foot off the ground | even low obstacles force going around | sprinting is a lot slower than the ai team-mates- they always pull ahead even though you are supposed to follow them | this character motion problem is a little subtle but very noticible after just playing other shooters with much better character control | at first i thought maybe something was wrong on my machine until i watched a playthrough of a level i just completed on youtube | same thing- slightly slow-motion compared with the rest of the game ememies team-mates and etc | not enough ammo forcing switching guns frequentore ly with fallen enemies | this is also very 'death-match'ish' and lessens the realism as the last thing a real soldier wants on the battlefield is to pick up and use an unfamiliar weapon | to make it worse the guns of fallen enemies dissappear pretty quickly | i finally gave up on the game during a follow-me type of sequence | you are supposed to 'sneak' through this survivalist camp in broad daylight while 'insane survivalists' are walking all around | the game hint says to follow this team-mate and stay low | after about four times of literally following so close we were touching i gave up | the scenario is so- well dumb | broad review_text: i've been thinking about how to review this game ever since i heard of the steam release | i've played this game for a very long time dating back to when nexon was publishing the game and ran it into the ground | i'm a bit of a fanatic you see | i think it's only fair that i criticize the game as harshly as i can muster to present a realistic representation of it | you should know in advance that in spite of its many shortcomings i still recommend it because there's nothing else quite like it on the market | the only games that have come close shut down long before an english translation was even in the realm of possibility because neople pretty much has a monopoly on this specific subset of online brawlers | anyway on to the meaty stuff | the interface is terrible | it's not uncommon for games of korean origin to have confusing interfaces that simultaneously overload you with information while simultaneously failing to deliver critical information when you need it | to be fair to neople they've done a lot to clean it up since its initial launch | but i've recommended this game to a few of my friends and an increasingly common complaint is the interface | the moment you login you're bombarded with notifications about events that you have no appreciation or understanding of before you even know how to move your character manage your inventory attack the monsters and use your skills | i personally don't have a problem parsing the visual overload but i've been playing this game whenever it's available in english since the original nexon release several years ago | controller support is rubbish | it technically works it automatically detects dpads and analog sticks so you can move around right away | but no other button is bound meaning you have to go through and manually bind jump attack two skill activator buttons skill hotkeys item slots and several other buttons possibly before you even know that you'll be expected to use them | no effort has been made on neople's part to adapt the interface to better suit controllers or even provide default bindings for common controllers like xinput devices which adds a lot of setup time to your first launch | to really play the game with as little keyboard and mouse interaction as possible most players rely on external programs like xpadder since it allows you to macro things up in a way that the game itself does not support | again not a problem for a diehard fan like me that already knows how to play the game but it presents a significant barrier to someone new to this game that claims partial controller support on the store page | the bulk of your leveling experience will be spent snoring your way through dungeons that are too easy | it's not until much later that you'll unlock access to higher difficulties for scenario dungeons which could lead to many players getting bored of the game before they get to see what it really has to offer | a big point in neoples' favor is that once you acclimate to the game there's a ton of content on offer nearly limitless dungeons to explore dozens of completely different playable characters to explore them with and multiple systems in place that encourage you to play more than one character too | the in-game shop is generous with its pricing on non-cosmetic items letting you buy valuable perks that affect long-term gameplay like stash space for pennies on the dollar | many events that they run shower you with premium items and avatars which means many people who treat this game as truly free to play can still play it without ever feeling the need to drop a dime | if you really want to differentiate yourself you will need to drop some real money on avatars or fork over in-game gold to other players that have done so already and there are ways for you to support the continued development of the game in the form of monthly subscription packs cosmetic perks and items that can slightly alleviate certain end-game specific grinds | i don't know if neople putting this game on steam will get them the revenue they're expecting | but i'll certainly be doing my part to spread the word and continue to support this one of a kind game |

see other players but all the fighting is done in instanced dungeons | i prefer that because it allows it to be a bit more challenging and execution heavy than a 'real' mmo | it's got a really wide variety of classes to choose from a massive amount of content thanks to being like a decade old and a combat system that's easy to pick up while also having a lot of complexity | it's free to play dragon's crown basically | except it came out before dragon's crown | now there are some problems with dfo | it's run by some korean guys in a company called neople and bless their ing hearts they try their hardest at this but they're more or less running a korean game with korean design and korean ideas but hosted in naeu with an english translation | this leads to some parts of the game looking that bad | the first hurdle you're going to have to jump is the fatigue system | basically you get x amount of fp every day and once you run out you can't play anymore until tomorrow | most people probably see this and flash back to mobile scam games that let you play for minutes then ask you to pay for more game time | this isn't dfo's case though | you can't exactly pay for more fp | you can fp entirely | which means you can technically play forever | and even if you're hard maining a character you want an alt | because having an alt gives so many bonuses that ignoring them is stupid | they give you flat stat boosts depending on how many decently leveled alts you have you can send them on missions to generate some loot and you can summon them as supports in dungeons | the next thing you might notice is that avatars give stat boosts | just know that you can buy rare avatars ones with increased stat bonuses for a not entirely unreasonable price off the auction house | or you could get the current box set of advanced avatars slightly worse stats than rare avatars at usually a pretty dang reasonable price and that often includes a pet and a special title | so it's a weird system is basically a weird alt currency that you get passively for completing dungeons | ] what i'm getting at is this game is really rng | that's all mmorpg's especially korean ones but i'm just giving you fair warning | of course you don't have to worry about that at all for a long time so the only reason this would affect you is if you get really really into it | also good news is that chronicle or timed but you can make them permanent with an item also purchasable with mileage points | free skill reset | don't like your skill setup | reset it | free of charge | class change until level | don't in-game currency gold | this game requires skill | while some classes are easier to use than others skillful play is definitely required to some degree | you can put skills onto hotkeys but you can also use key inputs | moreover you get better as you play even without realizing it and growing in skill feels really good | especially if you taught yourself the combos | events aren't paywalled | unlike some mmos that require you to crack open your wallet to fully participate in some events dfo events are almost always % free and very rewarding | bustling friendly community | if you're in the right channel for your level there is no shortage of players | the game feels alive and very busy | on top of that i've had nothing but good experiences with other players | yes a bitter unpleasant player passes through every so often but this game has had the most positive community i've seen in a long time with minimal shoutbox drama to boot | virtually grind-free | aside from grinding at endgame to get sweet gear level progression is pretty well organized | following the story quests and picking up any subquests you find will easily prepare you for whatever dungeon comes next | devs unfortunately the charm is only skin deep and the different systems in the game have been simplified so much since the game's initial release | when you first make a character you're led through a review_text: tl;dr think god of war lite | not deep; simple and fun | buy it if it's on sale | having never played the first force unleashed i can't of course compare the two which has its advantages and disadvantages | i think the biggest problem i ran into having missed the first installment was being thrust into the middle of a plot that desperately requires context | playing all the way through allowed me to put together many of what i presume to be major plot points from the first game but the lack of background for every character except vader made the plot feel pretty shallow | at first i thought the two main characters promised to be pretty likeable throughout the banter between starkiller and the general being playful and enjoyable at least initially | i sort of expected a character like starkiller to fulfill a stereotype that would suit any year old darksider of that name; gutteral voice brooding angst and a hood worn far too low over the face | i was pleasantly surprised to find starkiller's demeanor to be far more relateable and altogether human | a little over halfway through the game after listening to the old jedi and the young jedi bicker like a married couple each pouting and throwing fits at various intervals their personalities began to grate on me | i found the most overall pleasant character to be the love interest and she was offscreen roughly % of the game | to be honest though our two protagonists were still much less flat and unlikeable than i expected so i can't be too harsh | as far as gameplay is concerned it wasn't anything particularly unique | it felt like a hack n' slash with superpowers think god of war but less interesting | i think all of your force powers are unlocked within the first quarter of the game which meant that you had plenty of time to master and upgrade the ones you wanted and ignore the ones you didn't but unfortunately there wasn't really enough of a selection to make combat really feel like your own | you are given virtually no variability as far as melee combos which is a little disappointing since i occasionally like to feel like i'm doing more than just mashing the attack button until a finishing move happens | the game tries to present the player with some customization with the unlockable saber crystals but honestly once i locked in the ones that gave me more force points i didn't even bother anymore | i will readily acknowledge the pleasure in using force powers to mow down scores of stormtroopers turn lightsaber wielding baddies against their friends and redirect projectiles at whatever other enemy the arbitrary targeting system for force throw decides go for which is another gripe i have | the inclusion of quicktime events as all but mandatory is frustrating | getting to watch our hero dismember robots in spectacular ways is very very cool;
